newsitem.title: USA: True North in talks to acquire Bozell Jacobs.
newsitem.headline: True North in talks to acquire Bozell Jacobs.

text.p: True North Communications is in talks to acquire rival advertising agency New York-based Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon & Eckhardt in a stock swap valued at more than $375 million, sources close to the talks said Tuesday.
Only a few details have yet to be worked out, according to the sources, who declined to be identified.
If completed, Bozell would operate as a separate agency network under the Chicago-based True North corporate umbrella.
Although an agreement appears to be near, the deal could still fall through, sources inside both companies said.

True North's board met Friday but a spokeswoman for the company said the meeting was "purely informational" and that "no decision has been made." A source inside Bozell said, "We're listening, but no deal is imminent."

One of the details remaining is the resolution of an apparent conflict between Bozell's major client, Chrysler Corp., and the estimated $240 million Mazda Motor of America account at Foote Cone & Belding, True North's single advertising agency network. Although talks have taken place with Chrysler, "there has never been any decision made over what to do with Mazda," the source said, adding, "it is not an impediment to the deal."
Executives at True North and Bozell declined to comment on the ongoing talks.
True North, headed by Bruce Mason, has acquired about 20 smaller agencies since it ended its alliance with its French partner Publicis earlier this year.
"He's been very acquisition-minded," the source familiar with the talks said of Mason. "He said he wants multiple agency network brands under the True North banner."
True North had worldwide billings of $889.5 million last year, while Bozell's were $473.1 million, according to Advertising Age magazine.
True North's stock closed at $22 a share, up 62.5 cents, on the New York Stock Exchange.
